Teaching Objectives
Explore, describe, and interpret data in their multidimensional aspect.
Prerequisites:
Basic knowledge of descriptive statistics and matrix calculus.
Course Content (21h)
Chapter 1 – Introduction to Data Analysis
Definition and objectives of exploratory analysis
Data typology: qualitative, quantitative, ordinal
Steps of a data analysis project
Data preparation: cleaning, coding, handling missing values
Chapter 2 – Analysis of Relationships Between Variables
Correlation analysis (Pearson, Spearman)
Dependency test between qualitative variables (chi-square)
Analysis of variance (ANOVA)
Simple and multiple linear regression: interpretation, goodness of fit
Chapter 3 – Factor Analysis
PCA – Principal Component Analysis (for quantitative data)
CA – Correspondence Analysis (contingency tables)
MCA – Multiple Correspondence Analysis (multiple qualitative variables)
MFA – Mixed Factor Analysis (mixed qualitative and quantitative variables)
Chapter 4 – Data Classification
Hierarchical Ascending Classification (HAC)
Partition methods: k-means, k-medoids
Choosing the number of classes (Calinski-Harabasz, silhouette criteria, etc.)
Group interpretation and class visualisation
Chapter 5 – Data Visualisation
Univariate charts: histograms, boxplots, pie charts
Bivariate charts: scatter plots, correlation matrices
Multidimensional visualisation: factor maps, individual projection
Interactive visualisation with Python (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly) or R (ggplot2, FactoMineR)
Chapter 6 – Time Series
Deterministic modelling
Trend analysis
Moving averages
Decomposition of a time series
Forecasting by exponential smoothing
Chapter 7 – Case Studies and Applications
Application on real datasets (marketing, health, education, etc.)
Complete guided exploratory analysis
Method selection according to data nature
Critical interpretation of statistical results
Mini-project in pairs or groups
Assessment
Final examination (in person): 60%
Continuous assessment (CC): 40% — tests, personal work
